doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teddy Wilson and Tatum as influences, and lessons with Lennie Tristano
summary: She took a lesson or two with Tristano when she and Jimmy first came to New York; he told her to practice with a metronome because her time was erratic, and she found it valid.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: One aspect, just going back, I want to stay where you are in this lineage. We’ve talked about some of the people who came before you in regard to Duke Ellington and maybe some of the others, Teddy Wilson certainly, that came . . .
Teddy and Art Tatum were big influences on me.
Yes. Was someone, and these can be little quick short answers, influenced, say someone like Lennie Tristano?

Yes. As a matter of fact I went and took . . . I took a lesson or two with Lennie Tristano. This was when Jimmy and I first came to New York. I thought he could help me improve my overall jazz playing. I’d heard that Bud Freeman went to him and took some lessons. Bud Freeman was saying how interesting . . . in fact it was written up in Down Beat, like it was a happening. Bud Freeman studies with Lennie Tristano. How bizarre can you be? Anyway, I thought I would go, and I went to see Lennie. I think I had met him in a club. I found him very forbidding. It wasn’t . . . It was like going to a church and seeing some kind of mysterious being. He asked me to play, and I played something. I don’t know what. And he . . . his criticism of my playing was that I had very erratic time. He

said, if you want to be a romantic kind of player who plays rubato and goes with the . . . you just flow back and forth, you don’t keep a steady rhythm, that’s fine. But if you want to be a jazz player and have good time, you better go home and play with the metronome. That was pretty much what he said. I was crushed, but I felt that it was a valid criticism, and I did that.
So it was, you felt it was productive, those two lessons or whatever it was.
